purpose: Execution specification for future work; no new simulation capability is implemented by these records.

starter_tickets.title: Freeze the historical baseline and define change control
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: The frozen documentation treats D1-D5 as closed, while ROADMAP_DIFF and executable comments identify weaker guarantees. The physics_build string is manually maintained and historical artifacts lack a complete execution identity.
starter_tickets.change: Identify an immutable 0.1 source revision and dependency environment, record artifact fingerprints and supported reproduction commands, and establish candidate/accepted build states. Preserve accepted historical data without representing the broader phase as complete.
acceptance: The manifest resolves to exact source and preserved 0.1 summary, decompressed log and hash-list fingerprints; validate hashes without rerunning the universe.
A current-status record distinguishes accepted BUILD0 microslice, known defects, proposed phase contracts and implemented-but-unvalidated changes.
The version policy names model, runtime, log, RNG and state schemas and requires new artifacts for changes that alter a trajectory or its interpretation.
No original audit or acceptance files are overwritten or silently replaced.

Classify every existing test as a shared invariant, legacy 0.1 characterization or domain-scoped model-validation check. Specify separate execution contexts before behavior changes and run legacy characterizations against the archived 0.1 source; no blanket xfail or weakened assertion hides a changed model.
starter_tickets.compatibility: This ticket is documentation/manifest work and must not alter 0.1 simulation outputs. Historical replay remains an isolated archived-source operation.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Add explicit run manifests and compatibility preflight
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: run_recorded currently records ticks, cells, hash interval, probes and jump flag. replay_dir primarily checks physics_build and reuses meta; source, constants, numerical/runtime identity and schema identity are not complete compatibility inputs.
starter_tickets.change: Emit a validated run manifest containing model/runtime identifiers, relevant source/configuration hashes, numeric policy, package versions, seed, scheduler settings and schema versions. Classify which fields affect exact replay and which are informational. Check compatibility before allocating a world or consuming events.
acceptance: Manifest round trips preserve semantic fields and reject missing required fields, unsupported schemas and contradictory settings.
Tests change a behavior-relevant constant/configuration, source/runtime fingerprint or RNG schema while retaining the old physics label; preflight fails before simulation.
Nonsemantic paths and timestamps do not enter simulation RNG coordinates or canonical state hashes.
Legacy 0.1 input is either supported by an explicitly compatible reader/executor or rejected with an archived-source reproduction instruction; no guessed migration is performed.
starter_tickets.compatibility: Adding metadata alone need not change the physical equations. The log schema must still change if its serialized header changes, and the compatibility policy must preserve historical verification boundaries.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Register current event kinds and stable event identities
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: Draw kinds live in constants.KIND_IDS, while collapse/jump kinds are separately declared in rng.LOG_KIND_IDS. Logs encode a truncated kind hash and generic payload digest; there is no global versioned semantic registry.
starter_tickets.change: Create a minimal registry for events actually implemented today, with unique stable IDs, schema versions, required payload fields, producer ownership and draw-versus-log-only role. Define stable process/species/channel/attempt identity for new events. Reserve an extension mechanism without fabricating future phase implementations.
acceptance: Duplicate IDs, conflicting names/schema versions, unregistered producers and missing required fields fail validation.
The same semantic event ID survives cache regeneration and deterministic channel re-enumeration.
Legacy encoding is identified separately; replacing truncated kind hashes does not pretend old logs use the new registry.
The initial registry contains only implemented kinds and documented extension points; S25 is marked partial foundation work, not closed for all future phases.
starter_tickets.compatibility: A registry/schema change requires explicit log compatibility. Event identity must be independent of wall-clock timing and incidental Python container order.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Give independent stochastic events distinct random addresses
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: EventContext.draws starts at (cell << 24) + (sub << 48) on every call. Condensation and removal calls for different species reuse prefixes at the same tick/kind/cell/sub; payload contents do not change the address. The public audit reproduces identical prefixes for requests of length 10 and 16 with different payloads.
starter_tickets.change: Introduce explicit logical draw addresses containing stable event/process identity and a draw offset. Define supported bounds, overflow and duplicate-range behavior, deterministic byte encoding and generator/hash collision assumptions. Allocate species/channel identities explicitly rather than use a global call-order counter.
acceptance: The original repeated-prefix case is captured as a regression. Distinct logical events receive disjoint addresses; duplicate allocations are rejected in a diagnostic mode.
Chunking one draw range and reordering independent events produce the same addressed values; conditionally omitted work does not shift unrelated streams.
Scalar/vector implementations match new golden vectors, invalid address bounds fail clearly, and record/verify modes regenerate identical new-build histories.

A separately declared statistical test battery checks the chosen generator and application streams. Do not assert that all numeric outputs differ or that unique coordinates mathematically prove independence.
validation_commands_after_implementation: python -m pytest -q tests/test_rng.py tests/test_rng_addresses.py tests/test_log.py tests/test_replay.py
starter_tickets.compatibility: This changes trajectories. Advance the candidate behavior/RNG version and record new golden vectors without replacing 0.1 vectors or treating new final hashes as failures of historical reproduction.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Fingerprint the full causal state with a typed schema
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: Current fingerprints include sorted record columns and selected arrays, but do not include pool ordering, next-ID allocation, driver skip/bound/processed flags or freeze-tracking state that can affect later execution. IDs are converted to float64 and array byte order is native.
starter_tickets.change: Inventory authoritative versus derived state, move causal driver variables into a serializable state record, and hash explicit field names/types/shapes with a fixed byte-order policy. Preserve order where it affects future random selection; do not sort a causal pool merely to make hashes match.
acceptance: Changing each causal field independently changes the new fingerprint or fails a consistency invariant; purely diagnostic/informational fields follow the documented exclusion rule.
Integer identifiers remain lossless at their declared supported limits; type, length and endian encoding are explicit.
Equivalent serialization round trips produce identical fingerprints, including after cache reconstruction where cache contents are declared noncausal.
Document that a complete causal-state fingerprint is not yet a resumable checkpoint: pause/resume, I/O atomicity and version migration require their own later acceptance tests.
starter_tickets.compatibility: Use a new state/hash schema. Preserve original hashes as original-schema artifacts; never compare incompatible schema digests as though they measure physical drift.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Specify kinetic time and build a closed-box reference harness
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: The driver uses geometric physical-looking times but weak, nuclear and atomic kernels apply fitted per-tick probabilities without a consistent variable delta-t. Caps, a fixed draw budget and one-forward-or-reverse scheduling change effective kinetics. Several configured constants have no operative runtime use.
starter_tickets.change: Declare rate units, supported temperature/population domain, time-step mapping, reaction combinatorics and open/closed reservoirs. Implement a small independent reference for fixed-temperature finite systems, plus exact or analytically known stationary distributions. Keep expansion-driven cosmological claims outside this reference gate.
acceptance: A parameter ledger distinguishes operative constants, calibration inputs, mathematical constants, declared-but-unused fields and future placeholders.
Reference cases include a reversible finite A+B/C system and a one-charge capture/ionization system with exact inventory constraints.
Reference correctness is checked against analytic probabilities or an independently derived finite-state generator; the same production helper is not used on both sides of the comparison.

Numerical tolerance, supported domain, seed/sample protocol, error budget and calibration/held-out split are committed before inspecting candidate outcomes. No invented universal tolerance or arbitrary cosmology band is substituted.
Dimensionless/model-time use is clearly labeled if no defensible physical-unit mapping is yet selected.
starter_tickets.compatibility: This defines the candidate model contract. It must not retroactively reinterpret the time or rates of archived 0.1 records.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Enumerate reversible nuclear channels independently of populations
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: network._rates skips any pair with an absent forward reactant. A product-only (Z=1,A=2) state therefore lacks the reverse path to (1,1)+(0,1), although bind.channel_open accepts the forward channel. Other reactions may fire; the defect is the absent reverse edge.
starter_tickets.change: Build a canonical, bounded, reversible channel graph from allowed species and declared binding/stability rules. Store stoichiometry, reaction Q, canonical ID and forward/reverse availability separately from instantaneous population propensities. Preserve the distinction between imposed stability rules and derived energies.
acceptance: A product-only state contains the expected dissociation edge even with zero corresponding reactants; forward propensity is zero while a permitted reverse propensity can be positive.
Absent products do not remove an allowed forward edge. Canonical graph/cache reconstruction produces identical channel identities and order.
Duplicate unordered pairs and invalid species sums are rejected; every channel's A and Z stoichiometry balances exactly.
This PR demonstrates reachability/structure only; it does not claim correct equilibrium until D0-08 passes.
starter_tickets.compatibility: Graph enumeration changes event identities and potential histories; use the candidate build and regenerate only its references.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Derive paired nuclear propensities and validate the sampler
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: The reverse expression uses total product binding rather than channel Q, omits the forward charged-pair suppression, and combines capped probabilities with sequential if/elif updates. Identical-pair counting is ni*(ni-1), whose coefficient convention is not declared.
starter_tickets.change: Derive forward/reverse propensities from the selected equilibrium relation and declared microscopic counting convention. Implement the reference stepper for the bounded domain before any accelerated approximation. Separate equilibrium constants, kinetic prefactors and event sampling.
acceptance: For finite reference states, paired transitions satisfy the declared stationary relation, including product-only/reactant-only boundaries and identical reactants.
Reaction Q uses product minus reactant bindings; shared suppression/statistical factors follow the written derivation rather than a cosmetic formula substitution.

The sampler matches reference transition probabilities and stationary distributions under the predeclared protocol; test finite-population distributions rather than requiring their mean to equal a thermodynamic-limit formula exactly.
Conservation and nonnegative counts hold for every event, and event ordering/time refinement effects are bounded or explicitly part of the selected exact reference algorithm.
Stochastic tests use registered confidence/seed rules with deterministic structural tests as the primary regression checks; they are not 'some event eventually happens' assertions.
starter_tickets.compatibility: Expect changed yields. Do not retune or broaden old acceptance bands merely to regain green status; publish new-model results against frozen calibration and held-out cases.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Make the atomic state graph reversible at neutral and ionized boundaries
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: Fully captured species are excluded from channels; m_up = captured % n_tot also removes reverse moves at fully filled capture levels. T>T_GATE disables every update, so existing bound populations cannot ionize there. The archived 100-neutral-particle diagnostic records zero events while the internal Saha helper predicts positive ionization.
starter_tickets.change: Use an explicitly enumerated charge-state population representation for the supported model. Derive adjacent capture/ionization transitions and keep reverse moves available at full neutrality, including with zero free electrons. Declare what temperatures and charge states are supported; remove unjustified gating or return an explicit unsupported-domain result.
acceptance: Neutral, fully ionized and partially filled initial states have the correct nonzero/zero transition propensities at their boundaries, tested without dependence on lucky random draws.
The one-charge finite system relaxes from both ends to the same reference stationary distribution under D0-06's protocol.
Multi-charge inventory counts, occupancy and adjacent transition energies are explicit; no global multi-level equilibrium claim is made from the one-charge Saha formula.
Nuclear charge, bound/free electron inventory and nonnegative populations satisfy independent event accounting.
Summary metrics distinguish bound-electron fraction from neutral-particle number fraction; downstream code and test names use the correct definition.
starter_tickets.compatibility: This changes state serialization, kinetics and likely summary values. Version all affected schemas and the candidate model; keep 0.1 aggregate-state data readable only in its declared context.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Expose inventory transfers and model boundary accounting
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: Atomic free charge is currently derived algebraically from captured counts. The wider thermal/weak/bind pipeline uses prescribed baths and sea completion without an independently closed constituent charge, energy or entropy ledger.
starter_tickets.change: Add a small independent inventory accounting layer for repaired reaction events and declare external reservoirs/boundary inputs for the wider pipeline. Record known stoichiometric changes and modeled energy exchange; report unmodeled transfers as unsupported rather than invent equal-and-opposite entries solely to make residuals vanish.
acceptance: Nuclear and atomic closed-box event budgets independently reconstruct before/after inventory and catch a deliberately missing or doubled transfer.
The specification names which quantities are conserved in each control and which cross open boundaries in the expanding demo.
Sea-completion and thermal-bath limitations are represented explicitly in diagnostics; no global conservation claim is inherited from the atomic identity alone.
Rates/state changes and accounting records agree on units and event identity, with unsupported quantities visibly marked rather than silently treated as zero.
starter_tickets.compatibility: A new observational ledger can be metadata-only, but closing a missing physical transfer by changing model behavior is a separate versioned change. Full photon dynamics, baryogenesis and sea-completion replacement are outside this PR.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Replace quietness heuristics with explicit jump certificates
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: network.jump_quiet checks currently enumerated per-tick weights against 1e-8, while JUMP_SPAN is 1000. Nonzero hazard accumulates across channels/cells/intervals, and the existing graph omits reverse paths. One seed's identical final hash is not a universal proof.
starter_tickets.change: Keep jumping disabled for unsupported repaired kernels until they issue a certificate over the complete skipped interval. Exact mode requires zero omitted transition hazard. A distinct approximate mode must carry a conservative integrated bound, declared error budget, assumptions and invalidation conditions.
acceptance: Zero-hazard inert controls match detailed evolution exactly, including causal-state fingerprints and event semantics.
Any active, unknown, gate-crossing or uncertified interval refuses a jump; tests cover reverse-only and initially neutral cases.

Approximate certificates bound the integral of all possible omitted hazards over the interval under their stated assumptions, not only the current single-channel probability; accumulated run budget is checked separately.
Violation of a certificate's population, temperature, boundary or schema assumptions invalidates it before skipping.
Selected ensemble/reference comparisons test the declared observable error protocol; approximate jumps are never labeled bit-identical by construction.
starter_tickets.compatibility: The conservative first implementation may retain only zero-hazard jumps or no jumps. Performance regression is reported honestly; later speedups require measurements and cannot weaken scientific gates.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

starter_tickets.title: Publish the new reference validation dossier and release decision
starter_tickets.problem_evidence: The current broad bands include tuning targets, permit zero D/H, and record Li/H without a predictive check. Prototype SoA throughput does not measure the actual dictionary-backed complete engine.
starter_tickets.change: Run the preregistered controlled and held-out studies, archive every result and failure, profile the complete reference workload, and decide whether the candidate qualifies for an accepted 0.2 baseline. Keep software verification, physical validity, numerical error, sampling uncertainty and runtime cost separate.
acceptance: All deterministic structural, compatibility, state, inventory and boundary regressions pass; new-build record/replay passes within each supported environment.
Held-out controls meet the prespecified tolerances and sample-size/power plan; calibration and evaluation cases are identified separately. Passing seeds are not selected after inspection.
Temperature, time-resolution, population-size and event-order studies quantify the supported domain. Rare-species zeros are reported with counting limitations, not treated as abundance validation.
The dossier includes manifests, machine-readable metrics, uncertainty methodology, reference comparisons, known failures and run/storage costs for the actual engine.
Windows/Linux CI passing is not advertised as cross-platform complete-hash identity unless that comparison is explicitly performed and supported.
Acceptance is withheld if a core gate fails. Only after passing does the release mark the new baseline accepted and unlock the next Phase 1 work package.
validation_commands_after_implementation: python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider  # active suites after D0-01 test-scope migration
starter_tickets.compatibility: New 0.2 results are compared scientifically with 0.1 where definitions permit, not forced to equal old bit traces. Do not overwrite historical artifacts or make release labels claim completion of all ROADMAP Phase 0 requirements.
starter_tickets.test_scope_policy: Candidate commands require the D0-01 shared/legacy/reference test inventory. Historical characterizations execute in the archived 0.1 source environment, not unmodified against changed kernels.

phases.title: World rules
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Specify the actual quant representation, IDs, pool order and canonical state. Treat a future SoA layout as a separately tested implementation change, not an existing fact.
Publish the effective field/model domain, calibrated inputs, structural rules and intended downstream observables. Require a named error/validation claim for each approximation.
Versioned run manifest: source revision, model constants and digest, physics build, RNG/event/state schemas, environment/runtime fingerprint and complete run configuration.
Define physical measurement/state transitions, numerical refinement and rendering separately. Keep the external probe fixture until a validated world-generated observation source exists.
Specify the global clock, dimensional time/rate convention, quiet-interval validity and exact-versus-approximate comparison policy.
Retain historical array microbenchmark; add representative engine profiling before deriving any production budget.
Retain the fitted shell experiment as calibration/feasibility evidence; document training and held-out sets without promoting it to an atomic solver.
Preserve existing replay and reduced-physics acceptance evidence, then add targeted characterization tests for gaps and a versioned successor baseline.

dependencies: Existing 0.1 source and archived runs
Operational status/provenance schema
Explicit compatibility and model-change policy before altered stochastic behavior
acceptance: A clean supported environment reproduces the preserved 0.1 acceptance run and verifies its saved event/hash trace; incompatible schemas fail with an actionable message.
The successor run manifest identifies every input needed to rerun its declared model; metadata-only checks are distinguished from complete checkpoints.
Distinct logical stochastic events have distinct versioned addresses, while re-requesting the same logical event yields the same draws.
Product-only and fully neutral characterization cases expose the existing reverse-path gaps; successor kernels pass their declared reachability and equilibrium tests.
The status registry cannot label a phase accepted without required evidence and closed prerequisite gates.
limits: The milestone is trustworthy reduced-model infrastructure, not a Standard Model or full quantum universe.
A global charge/energy assertion requires explicit bath and conversion-boundary accounting; algebraic electron-ledger closure alone is insufficient.
D1-D5 closure in historical documents does not override contrary executable evidence.

phases.title: Quantum layer
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Array-based quant store, stable address mapping, snapshot serialization and representative benchmarks; preserve semantic IDs and deterministic pool/event ordering.
Effective field and interaction kernels under an explicit model contract; population generation and interaction rules distinguish metadata from dynamics.
Tier scheduler and region summaries with validity intervals, invalidation rules, retained budgets and observable-error tests.
Observation/collapse rules and controlled interference cases against a declared reference quantum model; threshold transitions alone are not enough.
Explicit joint-state/correlation representation, graph invariants and semantic RNG addresses; test marginals and non-signalling independently of a chosen correlation score.
Probe fixture and field-only acceptance harness, plus a separately named compatibility/integration harness retaining the existing micro-seed nuclei/capture modules.

dependencies: Phase 0 successor baseline and compatibility policy
Approved quantum-model scope before W4/W5
W1 and W2 can proceed in parallel after contracts; W3 consumes their stable interfaces; W4/W5 follow relevant state and scheduler contracts; W6 integrates
acceptance: Store serialization round-trips complete declared state, including allocation/pool/scheduler state if checkpoint resumption is claimed.
Controlled interference and correlation tests match an independently specified model; no-signalling marginals and measurement settings are part of the test definition.
Randomized schedule and observation fixtures preserve the declared replay contract; approximate tier comparisons meet preregistered observable tolerances.
Actual integrated storage/logging cost is measured with hardware and workload recorded; historical spike numbers are not reused as engine throughput.
The Phase 1 to 2 interface identifies readable state and the sole binding-event write path.
limits: PHASE1 definition excludes nuclei while W6 demands H/He/Li. Resolve this by separating the field-only engine gate from the retained micro-seed integration gate.
Graph edges plus scalar per-quant phase do not establish a general entangled-state model.
Do not require the proposed 50 ns/quant or 20 ns/event thresholds in Python without a measured implementation/hardware budget.

phases.title: Nuclear layer
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Effective nucleon/residual-strong/Coulomb kernels and explicitly accounted constituent conversion; document calibration rather than infer force emergence from filtered baryon enumeration.
Binding/excitation records over a declared nuclide domain, reproducible computation/cache, disjoint calibration and prediction sets.
Reversible fusion channels with channel Q, physical propensities and finite-population combinatorics; reacting-region reduced evolution with quantified error.
Fission and decay channels, stability/termination rules, explicit supported modes and rate uncertainties.
Radiation transport/deposition records coupled to explicit matter/energy ledgers and declared spectral/species scope.
Nuclear acceptance, bounded-domain fuzz, stellar-cell yield experiment and frozen nuclide/radiation interface for atoms.

dependencies: Verified Phase 1 event/state interfaces
Successor baseline reversible-rate and conservation contracts
W1/W2 development can overlap; W3 needs both, W4 needs binding/excitation, W5 uses transition products, W6 integrates
acceptance: Prespecified held-out binding/structure set is evaluated separately from the five-anchor fit; unsupported nuclides return explicit states rather than fabricated values.
Every intended reverse channel remains reachable from product-only initial states and small closed networks match reference stationary distributions.
Per-event baryon number, charge and energy including emitted/absorbed bath terms close to stated numerical tolerances.
Rate-bucket, timestep and population convergence are measured; decay fuzz terminates or reports an explicitly supported stable/metastable state.
A stellar-yield source includes initialization, build, seed, log and uncertainty before any Phase 7 disk composition may consume it.
Cache-off evaluation reproduces the chosen model's outputs; the nuclide and radiation APIs have typed units and uncertainty fields.
limits: Loose half-life bands are initial-model limits, not predictive accuracy.
No blanket arbitrary-temperature/density or full nuclear chart support without a declared domain.
The source's 10-cm shielding example must specify source spectrum and material; it is not a universal radiation acceptance condition.

phases.title: Atomic layer
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Radial solver and documented correction hierarchy with grid/convergence error and explicit failed/unbound cases.
Species records and derived ionization, affinity, radius, occupancy and bonding descriptors over a declared Z/ion range.
Spectral energies and declared transition/intensity approximations; versioned read-only line/opacity inputs.
Reversible ionization/recombination with consistent bath terms, charge accounting and explicitly supported equilibrium/non-equilibrium regimes.
Atomic acceptance, held-out curves/spectra, fuzz, cache regeneration and chemical species interface.

dependencies: Validated nuclear record and radiation interface for integrated acceptance
Analytic/recorded nuclear fixtures may unblock isolated solver development but must remain labeled fixtures
W2-W4 consume W1; W5 integrates derived records and spectra/plasma
acceptance: Hydrogenic reference states and grid-refinement studies verify the numerical solver independently of fitted many-electron targets.
Held-out ionization, affinity and spectral cases quantify errors and correction-ladder use; all published records identify model and error status.
Closed-box ionization tests approach the same reference distribution from neutral and ionized starting states across the supported temperature/density domain.
Species caches can be removed and recomputed with identical results within the declared implementation contract.
Chemistry receives both electron occupancy and separately defined bonding-capacity descriptors; charge equals nuclear charge minus electron count.
limits: The source conflates oxygen's valence-electron count with common bonding valency; the operational schema must separate these quantities.
A proposed numerical cutoff or solver failure is not evidence that the periodic table ends at that Z.
Spherical effective orbitals and energy differences alone do not guarantee molecular or spectroscopic accuracy.

phases.title: Chemistry
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Bounded bond/interaction models consuming atomic records, with declared treatment of ionic, covalent and metallic regimes.
Molecular geometry, directional bonding and intermolecular terms with tested graph/geometry canonicalization.
Channel discovery, barrier models, reversible event sampling, electron transfer and surface intermediates; extend the allowed channel ontology for S10 templates and S12 photoexcitation.
Thermodynamic and phase records, solubility and acid/base calculations within a supported domain; expose the aggregate/self-assembly interface required by S11.
Polymer/catenation and organic reactor stress cases with independent data; report distributions and unknown pathways.
Conservation/domain fuzz, previously unseen graph cases, cache-off replay and species/reaction interface acceptance.

dependencies: Validated atomic energies/densities and nuclear charge/radius for integrated use
W1 to W2 to W3; W4/W5 overlap after core reaction contracts; W6 integrates
S12 kernel can use typed prescribed photon-flux fixtures before Phase 6 exists; its later integration must consume the actual Phase 6 flux contract
acceptance: A narrowly declared molecule/reaction domain matches held-out structure, energy and kinetic references after calibration is frozen.
Enumerated reversible pairs satisfy the specified equilibrium relation and remain reachable from every intended admissible initial state.
Every event preserves atoms, charge and accounted energy; invalid graphs and unsupported searches produce explicit results.
S10: a template accelerates formation of its complement relative to matched non-template/non-catalytic controls, with no direct product injection.
S11: aggregate/cell interfaces and concentration-ramp fixtures support measured assembly kinetics in the owning chemistry/materials kernels.
S12: photochannels consume a typed spectral flux, account for photon energy, and produce an on/off photolysis difference in the declared reference system.
A new-species test checks supported behavior without pre-populating the registry; it does not claim exhaustive chemistry.
limits: Local valence rearrangement is not a completeness proof. A missing candidate must not silently mean a physically impossible reaction.
The Haber example's H3 expression needs correction before it becomes a test fixture; use a balanced declared reaction.
Internal equilibrium consistency does not validate missing pathways, rates or the barrier approximation.
Chemistry may be developed in bounded stages; a universal reaction engine and pharmaceutical prediction are not the first deliverable.

phases.title: Materials and substances
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Material aggregation records, canonical signatures and explicit composition/phase/history provenance.
Phase and nucleation/growth kinetics, including S3 aerosol-mediated condensation and S11 amphiphile assembly where those mechanisms belong.
Mechanical property tensors, deformation history and fracture-energy closure over a bounded material domain.
Geological processing paths, compaction, weathering, melt behavior and creep constitutive inputs for later continuum physics.
Thermal/electrical transport, viscosity, diffusion and permeability with uncertainty and supported regimes.
Progressive material manifest, history fuzz, bounded summaries, cache regeneration and material/deformation contracts.

dependencies: Validated chemistry and phase/energy interfaces
W1 is root, W2 feeds W3-W5; W3/W4/W5 can overlap after interfaces; W6 integrates
Primitive fixture material records can support independent continuum unit tests without claiming real derived properties
acceptance: Begin with a declared small material family; expand the source's 100-material manifest only as supported regimes and independent data become available.
History changes produce reproducible property changes and appropriately measured hysteresis; bounds and cache keys retain all declared sufficient statistics.
Summary reconstruction is compared to detailed/reference material calculations on selected observables with fixed tolerances.
S3: aerosol-on/off and concentration/temperature ramps test vapor nucleation kinetics and water/latent-energy accounting.
S11: assembly yields and rupture/persistence responses are tested against declared concentration-ramp reference cases.
Mechanical and transport predictions are tested on held-out processing conditions, not just the fitted anchor values.
Deformation and thermal exposure enter through logged events; caller code cannot directly overwrite material properties.
limits: Materials are not the only lossy layer; the same closure discipline applies to later planet, population and institutional summaries.
A direction-only conductivity or doping trend is insufficient evidence for later semiconductor/circuit operation.
A few-hundred-particle reference is not automatically representative of a macroscopic constitutive property.

phases.title: Continuum physics
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Conserved-field layout, transport, stability/substepping and gravity; add rotating-frame support S1 and a versioned gravity-constant decision S4/S9.
Conduction/advection/phase energy coupling and entropy/export accounting, including valid resumed coarse intervals.
Contact, stress and fracture, extended by geological viscoelasticity S2 and later articulated rigid-body coupling S13.
Radiation/line transport and typed spectral flux interfaces consumed by chemistry and perception.
Pressure observations and explicitly scoped electromagnetic regimes; later circuit/near-field/radio support is S15 rather than an automatic consequence of magnetostatics.
Component and coupled acceptance, conservation/stability fuzz, bounded jump comparisons and the boundary-event interface S8.

dependencies: Material properties and logged-deformation interface
Atomic spectral and chemical phase/energy interfaces
W1/W2 can overlap; W3 needs kinematics, W4 uses thermal/radiative state, W5 couples relevant flow/EM terms; W6 integrates
acceptance: Analytic/reference transport, conduction, wave and two-body cases demonstrate conservation and refinement convergence in a declared regime.
CFL/adaptive-step and finite-state guards fail deliberately unstable fixtures rather than silently repairing them.
S1 rotation sign and geostrophic balance; S2 creep/relaxation and Rayleigh-crossing cases; S4 gravity units and orbit calibration each have upstream tests.
Heat, work, latent terms, radiation and exports reconcile over complete budgets; apparent closed-system entropy decreases must be accounted for or rejected.
Boundary changes are typed, logged events with deterministic ordering and provenance; direct lower-state edits fail an interface test.
Reduced-versus-detailed comparisons use per-observable tolerances and validity intervals unless mathematical equality for a particular kernel is established.
limits: The original general hash-transparency claim for nonlinear coarse physics is too strong.
A massless field label, group photon transport or magnetostatic operator does not supply every EM/circuit regime.
Shape-only agreement is useful but cannot replace quantitative error bounds needed by a downstream application.

phases.title: Planet and space
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Orbiting-body/ring summaries, accretion events and lazy astronomy over the shared gravity model; source/version the seeded disk and expansion clock.
Differentiation, mantle rheology and planetary magnetic summaries with declared closure regimes.
Tectonic boundary events, recycling, uplift and weathering fluxes through lower-layer APIs.
Resolved ocean/air/water-cycle feedbacks; later local tracer extension S20 belongs to this producer, not a downstream social workaround.
Abiotic reservoir graph and species/aerosol fluxes with photochemistry S12; producer attribution S19 must survive the same transport interfaces.
Versioned stellar/radiation boundary input generated by a supported lower model, including dose and spectral provenance.
Planet/environment integration, layered-resolution reconciliation, logged initialization, long-time convergence and environment/flux interface acceptance.

dependencies: Relevant Phase 2 stellar yield/radiation, Phase 5 material and Phase 6 physics interfaces
S1-S5/S8/S9 before the consumers that require them; D6/S6 before disk initialization; S7 implemented during planetary resolution work; S12 before W5
W1 then W2 then W3; W4 depends on physical rotation/nucleation and terrain/orbits; W5 consumes rain/weathering; W6 can overlap on a supported stellar fixture; W7 integrates
acceptance: Begin with one bounded region/planet and explicit boundary forcing before attempting the proposed multi-Gyr demonstration.
Resolve S5 with a versioned timeline/expansion model and independent reference cases, not a post-hoc date multiplier.

S6/D6 integrated acceptance requires a logged offline Phase 2 stellar-yield run from this engine, with seed/build/source identity, units and conserved inventory; cache-off regeneration must reproduce the consumed composition. Synthetic composition fixtures support isolated development only and do not close S6 or the integrated Phase 7/Great Run gate. Changing that source requirement requires an explicit scope-changing ADR.
S7: random promotion/demotion and shock windows preserve declared mass/species/energy budgets and meet predeclared observable errors.
S12-backed photolysis on/off produces accountable reservoir differences; climate and water budgets close with explicit boundary exports.
Long-horizon results report uncertainty, conservation drift, timestep/resolution sensitivity and failed outcomes; the environment read API and flux-only write path are tested.
limits: S6 and S7 are work within this phase, not reasons to demand all S1-S9 closed before any planetary unit work can start.
Snowball, runaway, lack of tectonics or absent life can be legitimate outcomes; do not automatically label an unwanted narrative a numerical bug.
A prior-generation seeded composition preserves provenance but is not evidence that all prior cosmic history emerged in the same run.
The proposed roughly 10,000 resolved cells and 4-Gyr wall-time targets are not measured capacities.

phases.title: Life and ecosystems
phases.entry_rule: D0 plus approved local model/interface contracts; fixtures may support isolated development

work_packages.description: Template/catalysis mechanism and read-only closure detector; explicit replication fidelity, variation and lineage records.
Compartment assembly/persistence, population records with necessary correlations and deterministic individual sampling.
Resource uptake and metabolism with explicit energy/work/heat/waste accounting and impossible-budget negative controls.
Food webs, decomposition and mutualistic exchanges through the same planetary flux graph; no direct environment-state edits.
Host-parasite and inhibitor/resistance experiments with conditional hypotheses and correlation-aware population state.
Regulatory/collective organization, bodies and sensory transduction; supported light harvesting and desiccation responses.
Integrated biological/environment experiments, population-to-individual validation, certified temporal reduction and the single-clock life/agent interface.

dependencies: S10 templating, S11 assembly and S12 photochannel interfaces, with the relevant Phase 2 radiation and Phase 4-6 energy/mechanics producers

W1 may start in an explicitly controlled chemistry fixture before complete Phase 7; W2 needs W1/S11; W3 needs compartments and actual environment input for integration; W4-W6 consume those contracts; W7 integrates
Integrated phase acceptance depends on a validated Phase 7 environment, not merely a prepared toy fixture
acceptance: Templating and catalysis controls establish a measurable mechanism; an autocatalytic closure detector must not inject species or modify the system it measures.
Show persistence, heritable variation and competition separately; explicitly seeded replicators are permitted only as declared experimental initialization, not evidence of abiogenesis.
Individual samples reproduce declared population and correlation statistics within predeclared sampling uncertainty; shock windows trigger detailed evolution or invalidate compression.
Biological fluxes reconcile with the same material/resource budgets used by the abiotic environment; impossible fixtures fail rather than receive hidden resources.
Host-parasite, cooperation and inhibitor outcomes are measured over controlled ensembles; stable, extinct and failed-emergence cases remain valid recorded results.
A supported light spectrum and biochemical coupling justify harvesting tests; no unsupported UV-B choice is silently treated as universal photosynthesis.
The life/agent interface uses the global clock and logged physical actions; D8 validity limits and any seeded fallback are recorded before claiming the corresponding capability.
limits: Autocatalytic closure is not a complete operational definition of life.
No mutation-rate constant in code is not proof that all replication errors derive from radiation; error mechanisms and effective parameters must be declared.
Biological/body-plan emergence and a particular historical ordering are research outcomes, not guaranteed engineering consequences.
The 500-Myr compressed era remains an integration ambition; phase completion requires an explicit supported scope and cannot be rescued by scripting a desired event.
